name: Trial Lesson
description:
In this lesson, students are introduced to a Raspberry Pi and related electronic components such as Grove Pi, Buzzer and RGB Backlight. The instructor will also be sharing with students what Computational Thinking is and its importance. Students will be able to program their own customized pedestrian traffic lights by the end of this unit.

Programming Definitions:
Raspberry Pi: The Raspberry Pi is a tiny and affordable computer that you can use to learn programming through fun, practical projects. Because of its affordability and complexity, Raspberry Pi are highly used in tertiary education.

Computational Thinking:
The characteristics that define computational thinking are decomposition, pattern recognition/data representation, generalization/abstraction, and algorithms. By decomposing a problem, identifying the variables involved using data representation, and creating algorithms, a generic solution results. The generic solution is a generalization or abstraction that can be used to solve a multitude of variations of the initial problem.

name: Basic : Blockly Games
description: In this lesson, students are given 3 different blockly games to explore. The student will spend time going through each of the categories and familiarize themselves with the block-based programming layout. Students will be able to use Blockly to use iterative methods to systematically solve problems.

name: Basic 1 : Sequence & Buzzer
description:
In this lesson, students are given the following sensors to explore and complete their challenges: Buzzer with the new concept(s) taught to them.

Programming definitions:

Buzzer: The Buzzer is a type of electronic device that's used to produce a tone, alarm or sound.

Sequence: A sequence is an ordered list containing successive steps or functions for performing certain actions. It can be used in programming or as a simple set of instructions to achieve a result, like accessing an account on a website or creating a word processing document.

name: Basic 1 : Sequence & LCD
description:
In this lesson, students are given the following sensors to explore and complete their challenges: LCD with the new concept(s) taught to them.

Programming definitions:

LCD: The LCD (Liquid Crystal Display) is a type of flat panel display which uses liquid crystals in its primary form of operation. Sequence: A sequence is an ordered list containing successive steps or functions for performing certain actions. It can be used in programming or as a simple set of instructions to achieve a result, like accessing an account on a website or creating a word processing document.

name: Basic 1 : Repeat Loops
description:
In this lesson, students are given the following sensors to explore and complete their challenges: Buzzer and LCD with the new concept(s) taught to them. Programming definitions:

Loop: A loop describes the process of a software program or script repeats the same instructions or processes the same information over and over until receiving the order to stop. Repeat loops iterate over the members of a sequence in order, executing the block each time.

name: Basic 1 : Wait Until & Button
description:
In this lesson, students are given the following sensors to explore and complete their challenges: Buzzer, LCD screen and a button with the new concept(s) taught to them.

Programming Definitions:

Button: The pushbutton is a component that connects two points in a circuit when you press it.

Wait Until: The wait until () block is a control block and a stacked block. The block pauses its script until the specified boolean condition is true.

name: Basic 1 : IF Conditionals
description:
In this lesson, students will be given additional outputs, i.e. buttons. With a buzzer, LCD screen and two buttons, they are tasked to explore and complete their challenges with the new concept(s) taught to them.

Programming definitions:

If Else (Conditionals): An if-else statement in programming is a conditional statement that runs a different set of statements depending on whether an expression is true or false.

name: Basic 1 : Comparison Operators &  AND Operators & Ultrasonic Sensor
description:
In this lesson, students are introduced to a new sensor: an Ultrasonic sensor. Using this new sensor, students are tasked to complete their challenges with the new concept(s) taught to them.

Programming definitions:

Ultrasonic sensor: Ultrasonic sensors measure distances based on transmitting and receiving ultrasonic signals.

AND: The AND keyword is a logical operator, and is used to combine conditional statements

Comparison operators: They are operators that compare values and return true or false . The operators include: > , < , >= , <= , == , and !=

name: Basic 1 : WHILE Conditionals
description:
In this lesson, students will be given additional outputs, i.e. buttons. With an LCD screen and two buttons, they are tasked to explore and complete their challenges with the new concept(s) taught to them.

Programming definitions:

While Loop: It is a control flow statement that allows code to be executed repeatedly based on a given Boolean condition. The while loop can be thought of as a repeating if statement.

name: Basic 1 : Individual Student Projects
description: In this lesson, students are tasked to create two projects using the concepts they have learnt so far. The sensors that they will be using for their projects are as follows: an LCD screen, a buzzer, an ultrasonic sensor, and buttons.

name: Basic 2 : Sequence & Repeat Loops & Motor Driver
description:
In this lesson, students are introduced to a new output: Motor Driver. Using this new output, students are tasked to complete their challenges by using sequence, a programming concept that was taught previously.

Programming definitions:

Motor Driver: The Motor Driver is a controller that controls the direction and speed of up to 2 DC motors.

DC Motors: The DC motor is a rotary electrical machine that converts direct current electrical energy into mechanical energy

Sequence: A sequence is an ordered list containing successive steps or functions for performing certain actions. It can be used in programming or as a simple set of instructions to achieve a result, like accessing an account on a website or creating a word processing document.

Loop: A loop describes the process of a software program or script repeats the same instructions or processes the same information over and over until receiving the order to stop. Repeat loops iterate over the members of a sequence in order, executing the block each time.

name: Basic 2 : Branching & Color Sensor
description:
In this lesson, students are given the motor driver and colour sensor to complete their challenges with the new concept(s) taught to them. Programming definitions:

Color Sensor: The color sensor is a type of "photoelectric sensor" which emits light from a transmitter, and then detects the light reflected back from the detection object with a receiver.

Branching: Branching is a basic concept in computer science. It means an instruction that tells a computer to begin executing a different part of a program rather than executing statements one-by-one. Branching is implemented as a series of control flow statements in high-level programming languages. These can include: If statements For loops While loops Goto statements

name: Basic 2 : Sequence & Branching
description:
In this lesson, students are given the motor driver and ultrasonic sensor to complete their challenges with the new concept(s) taught to them.

Programming definitions:

Sequence: A sequence is an ordered list containing successive steps or functions for performing certain actions. It can be used in programming or as a simple set of instructions to achieve a result, like accessing an account on a website or creating a word processing document.

Branching: Branching is a basic concept in computer science. It means an instruction that tells a computer to begin executing a different part of a program rather than executing statements one-by-one. Branching is implemented as a series of control flow statements in high-level programming languages. These can include: If statements For loops While loops Goto statements

name: Basic 2 : Project Ideas
description:
In this lesson, students are given a Motor driver, buzzer and buttons to complete their challenges with the new concepts taught to them.

Brainstorming is method design teams use to generate ideas to solve clearly defined design problems.

name: Basic 2 : Simplicity
description:
In this lesson, students are given buttons and LCD to complete their challenges with the new concepts taught to them.

Understand the functionality of the LCD and do not overcomplicate the progress

name: Basic 2 : Game Design
description:
In this lesson, students are given color sensor, buttons and LCD to complete their challenges with the new concepts taught to them.

Plan and design a simple an interactive game

name: Basic 2 : Individual Student Projects
description:
In this lesson, students are tasked to create two mini projects and one final project using the concepts they have learnt so far. Students will be using various sensors that they have used so far to complete the projects.

Sensors: Button, LCD screen, Color sensor, Buzzer, Motor Driver

name: Intermediate 1 : Number Range
description:
In this lesson, students will devise a smart car which detects obstacles between a certain range by using an ultrasonic sensor and a motor driver.

Programming Definitions:

Range: The range of a set of data is the difference between the highest and lowest values in the set. To find the range, first order the data from least to greatest. Then subtract the smallest value from the largest value in the set.

name: Intermediate 1 : Variables &Touch Sensor
description:
In this lesson, students will deepen their knowledge of variables with the use of a button sensor. This lesson will test their knowledge as they use variables to complete their challenges.

Programming Definitions:

Variables: Variables are used to store information to be referenced and used by programs.

Random: Random is an important part of the configuration and evaluation of machine learning algorithms.

name: Intermediate 1 : Variables & Random Number
description:
In this lesson, students will be learning two important concepts in programming: Variables and Random. Variables and Random are two highly used concepts in programming games.

Programming Definitions:

Variables: Variables are used to store information to be referenced and used by programs.

Random: Random Numbers in programming are not really random. They are a sequence of "pseudo" random numbers that needs to be defined typically with a list.

name: Intermediate 1 : For Loop
description:
In this lesson, students will be learning one important concept in programming: For Loop. For Loop is a concept that is commonly used in object-orientated programming languages

Programming Definitions:

For Loop: For loop is used for iterating over a sequence (that is either a list, a tuple, a dictionary, a set, or a string).

name: Intermediate 2 : For Loop & Logical Thinking
description:
In this lesson, students are given the LCD and Button Sensor to complete their challenges with the new concept(s) taught to them.

Programming definitions:

For Loop: For loop is used for iterating over a sequence (that is either a list, a tuple, a dictionary, a set, or a string).

Logical Thinking: It is the process in which one uses reasoning consistently to come to a conclusion.

name: Intermediate 2 : List & Random Number
description:
In this lesson, students will be learning two important concepts in programming: List and Random. List and Random are two highly used concepts in programming games.

Programming Definitions:

List: A list is a collection that is ordered and changeable.

Random: Random Numbers in programming are not really random. They are a sequence of "pseudo" random numbers that need to be defined typically with a list.

name: Intermediate 2 : List & Logical Thinking
description:
In this lesson, students will deepen their conceptual knowledge in the list.

Programming Definitions:

List: A list is a collection that is ordered and changeable.

Logical Thinking: It is the process in which one uses reasoning consistently to come to a conclusion.

name: Intermediate 2 : List & Variable
description:
In this lesson, students learnt how to program a counter. Counters are highly prevalent and used in-game applications as a way to keep track of scores and also time.

Programming Definitions:

Counter: A program counter is a register in a computer processor that contains the address (location) of the instruction being executed at the current time. As each instruction gets fetched, the program counter increases its stored value by 1.

Integer variable: Counter is an integer variable used to keep track of the number of times a specific piece of code is executed.

name: Intermediate 2 : Function
description:
In this lesson, students will be using functions to manipulate their Buzzer and LCD. They will be given various challenges to test their understanding of this new concept.

Programming Definitions:

Function: A function is a unit of code that is often defined by its role within a greater code structure. Specifically, a function contains a unit of code that works on various inputs, many of which are variables, and produces concrete results involving changes to variable values or actual operations based on the inputs.

name: Intermediate 2 : Function With Arguments
description:
In this lesson, students will be using functions with arguments to manipulate their Buzzer and LCD. They will be given various challenges to test their understanding of this new concept.

Programming Definitions:

Function: A function is a unit of code that is often defined by its role within a greater code structure. Specifically, a function contains a unit of code that works on various inputs, many of which are variables, and produces concrete results involving changes to variable values or actual operations based on the inputs.

Arguments: An argument or a formal argument, is a special kind of variable, used in a subroutine to refer to one of the pieces of data provided as input to the subroutine. These pieces of data are the values of the arguments (often called actual arguments or actual parameters) with which the subroutine is going to be called/invoked. An ordered list of arguments is usually included in the definition of a subroutine, so that, each time the subroutine is called, its arguments for that call are evaluated, and the resulting values can be assigned to the corresponding parameters.

name: Intermediate 2 : Function With Return
description:
In this lesson, students will be using functions with a return to return the outcome. They will be given various challenges to test their understanding of this new concept.

Programming Definitions:

Function: A function is a unit of code that is often defined by its role within a greater code structure. Specifically, a function contains a unit of code that works on various inputs, many of which are variables, and produces concrete results involving changes to variable values or actual operations based on the inputs.

Arguments: An argument or a formal argument, is a special kind of variable, used in a subroutine to refer to one of the pieces of data provided as input to the subroutine. These pieces of data are the values of the arguments (often called actual arguments or actual parameters) with which the subroutine is going to be called/invoked. An ordered list of arguments is usually included in the definition of a subroutine, so that, each time the subroutine is called, its arguments for that call are evaluated, and the resulting values can be assigned to the corresponding parameters.

Return: A return statement ends the execution of a function, and returns control to the calling function.

name: Intermediate 2 : Function & Logical Thinking
description:
In this lesson, students will be using functions with a return to return the outcome. They will be given various challenges to test their understanding of this new concept.

Programming Definitions:

Function: A function is a unit of code that is often defined by its role within a greater code structure. Specifically, a function contains a unit of code that works on various inputs, many of which are variables, and produces concrete results involving changes to variable values or actual operations based on the inputs.

Arguments: An argument or a formal argument, is a special kind of variable, used in a subroutine to refer to one of the pieces of data provided as input to the subroutine. These pieces of data are the values of the arguments (often called actual arguments or actual parameters) with which the subroutine is going to be called/invoked. An ordered list of arguments is usually included in the definition of a subroutine, so that, each time the subroutine is called, its arguments for that call are evaluated, and the resulting values can be assigned to the corresponding parameters.

Return: A return statement ends the execution of a function, and returns control to the calling function.

Logical Thinking: It is the process in which one uses reasoning consistently to come to a conclusion.

name: Intermediate 2 : Final Intermediate Project Enhancement
description: In this lesson, students will be using all the concepts that have learnt. They will be given an opportunity to upgrade and improve their old projects. The students will be programming their final projects.

name: Intermediate 2 : Project Report
description: In this lesson, students will have finished their final project and will be working on a project report for their final project. The purpose of the report is to enable a student to be able to explain and illustrate the programs that they have created to layman individuals with no programming background, hence simulating the environment whereby they are programmers in the future pitching to their prospective customers/clients.

name: Advance 1 : Print
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to display characters on the screen.

Programming definitions:

Print: Python command to display characters on the screen. It is very versatile and more advanced techniques with this command will be introduced as we progress

name: Advance 1 : Variable and Operations
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to use variables in their codes to store values, compute results with operators and display their values. Students will also be briefly introduced to data type.

Programming definitions:

Variable: A variable is used to store a value that can be changed while the program runs. It can be given a customised name for easy referencing.

Data Type: The classification of a value such as string, integer, float, etc. Certain operators can only work on the certain data types. For example, an integer or float (number) can be divided but a string (text) can't.

Operator: Arithmetic and String Operators are used to compute results with variables or values, such as add, minus, etc. Python has specific symbols for various operators. Certain operators can only be used for a certain types of data.

name: Advance 1 : Type Casting and Input
description:
In this unit, students will learn more about the concept of data type. The data type of the value that a variable is storing affects what kind of operation it can perform. Students will also learn how to get inputs from the user through the keyboard to enable interactions.

Programming definitions:

Data Type: The classification of a value such as string, integer, float, etc. Certain operators can only work on the certain data types. For example, an integer or float (number) can be divided but a string (text) can't.

Type Casting: To convert from one data type to another. This is done to facilitate certain operations.

Input: Python command to get input from the keyboard.

name: Advance 1 : If Statement
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to use if-statements to perform logic, that is, trigger certain actions based on conditions.

Programming definitions:

Condition: A statement that returns only True or False. It is commonly used with if-statements (and subsequently with loops) to trigger actions to be performed.

If-elif-else: Logical constructs that form the core logic of most algorithms.

Comparison Operators: Comparison operators, also known as relational operators, are used in conditions to compute a True or False return, thereby triggering certain actions.

name: Advance 1 : For Loop
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to use for-loop to repeat codes. A for-loop counts from a starting number to an ending number and it is useful when you know how many times or what number range to repeat. You can also control the looping interval.

Programming definitions:

Range: The start to end number. The step in a range refers to the interval between the iterations.

For-loop: Python constructs for repeating within a range with specific intervals.

Break: Python command to exit from a loop at any instance without condition.

name: Advance 1 : Good Programming Habits
description:
In this unit, students will learn some basic steps to keep their codes more readable for ease of interpretation and debugging.

Programming definitions:

Comment: Descriptions that are included in the codes but not executed as commands.

Good Naming Convention:  Variable naming is an important aspect of making your code readable.

name: Advance 1 : While Loop
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to use while-loop to repeat codes. A while loop can be used to create infinite looping or a loop that terminates upon a condition.

Programming definitions:

While-loop: Python constructs for repeating a set of codes while a condition is True.

Break: Python command to exit from a loop at any instance without condition.

name: Advance 1 : List
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to use list to store a large number of data. List has running indices which, when combining with for-loops, simplifies bulk processing of data. This forms a very important part of many algorithms.

Programming definitions:

List: A data structure that stores values in a sequence.

Index: The position of each item in a list. It begins with 0 to an extremely large number (limited only by the computer hardware).

Length: The length of a list refers to the number of items in the list.

Append: To add an item to the end of a list.

Insert: To insert an item at any position of a list.

Pop: To remove an item from a list.

name: Advance 1 : String Manipulation
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to manipulate strings such as amending or extracting part of a string. Efficient string manipulation techniques are important parts of many algorithms.

Programming definitions:

Substring: Part of a string.

In Operator: Operator to check the existence of a substring in a string.

Length: Number of characters in a string. It includes invisible characters such as space, return key, etc.

Index: The position of a character in a string. It starts from 0 to length-1.

name: Advance 2 : Try-Exception
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to prevent their program from crashing due to execution errors. They can then choose to resolve such errors in their program.

Programming definitions:

Try-Exception: A Python construct to capture program crash cause by invalid execution of codes.

name: Advance 2 : Function
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to develop their program in modules call functions. Functions are useful in solution design as they break down the program into tasks. They can also be executed multiple times, thus, reducing the codes.

Programming definitions:

Function: A Python construct that groups a set of codes to accomplish specific tasks.

Parameter: Also known as an argument, an input parameter to a function is a value to be passed to it for processing.

Return: Results that are processed by a function are being passed back via a return statement.

Global Variable: A variable that is outside a function (in the main body of a program) but accessible by it.

Local Variable: A variable within a function is its local variable. A local variable is not accessible by other functions or in the main body.

name: Advance 2 : 2D List
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to create and manipulate a 2D list. 2D lists are useful for handling tabulated data or data that are represented on a 2D space.

Programming definitions:

Row and column: A 2D list can be viewed as a table with rows (horizontal streams of data) and columns (vertical streams of data).

Index: The position of each item in a list. A item in a 2D list will have a row index and column index, both of which begins at 0.

Length: A 2D list is implemented as a row of lists, each list has a column of items. The length of 2D list is, thus, the number of lists it contains (rows) and the length of each list is the number of items in it (columns). Note that it is possible for each row to have a list of different lengths.

name: Advance 2 : Dictionary
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to use dictionary. A dictionary is a storage type that allows the program to quickly access a value based on a unique key.

Programming definitions:

Key-value: A key is a unique identifier. It can be any single value (e.g. string, integer, float, etc) and is used to point to a value. A value in a dictionary can be more than a single value (e.g. a list, 2D list, etc)

Update: To add an item to a dictionary.

Pop: To remove an item from a dictionary.

name: Advance 2 : File IO
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to save data permanently to a file on the hard disk.

Programming definitions:

Open: A file can be opened in different modes (e.g. for reading, writing, etc).

Close: After opening, a file has to be closed to ensure all data are properly saved. Python performs file closing automatically in certain file I/O construct.

Read: To read data from a file.

Write: To save data to a file.

name: Advance 2 : File Pointer
description:
In this unit, students will learn about file pointer. A file pointer can be used to set the position in a file from which data will be read or at which written data will be written.

Programming definitions:

File pointer: A locator that exists when a file is opened. It remembers the last position where data has been read or written.

Tell: To extract the position of a file pointer.

Seek: To shift the file pointer to a location.

name: Advance 2 : Turtle
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to perform basic illustrations using Turtle library.

Programming definitions:

Turtle: A Python library with commands to perform basic illustrations.

Screen: The window for drawing.

Pen: A virtual setting (e.g. colour, line thickness, etc) is used to execute the drawing.

Pixel: The smallest visible unit of an illustration, which is equivalent to a dot on the screen. The screen size is measured in pixels.

name: Advance 2 : Project
description:
You have come far. With what you have learnt, you already have the knowledge to make amazing programs. So let's do something like a pro.

This project is a test of what you have learnt so far and the instructor will not be debugging your codes. You will be graded based on how well your program works.

name: Advance 3 : Class
description:
In this unit, you will learn about OOP concept using classes in Python.

Programming definitions:

OOP: Object-Oriented Programming is a programming paradigm based on the concepts of "objects".

Class: A template codes consisting of variables and methods (functions). In order to execute the codes in a class, an object has to be created from it.

Object: An instance of a class. Each object has its own set of variables and methods. Its methods can manipulate its own variables without elaborate passing of parameters.

Method: Another name for function.

name: Advance 3 : Class Variable
description:
In this unit, you will learn how to create and use class variables. Different from object variables, class variables will not be duplicated by each object and are accessible by all.

Programming definitions:

Class Variable: A variable that belongs to a class. There is only one copy of the variable and it is not duplicated when an object is instanced. Hence, it acts like a global variable to the objects.

name: Advance 3 : Static Method
description:
In this unit, you will learn how to create and use static method. A static method is often designed as a method that does not need to process the object variables and hence, the object variables are not passed to it by the default manner.

Programming definitions:

Static method: A function belonging to a class (instead of an object). There is only one reference to the method and no multiples are created when an object is instanced. Object variables are thus, not passed to it by default.

name: Advance 3 : Class Inheritance
description:
In this unit, you will learn about using multiple classes in the same program and how a class can inherit another so that it can make use of existing variables and methods while adding on its own.

Programming definitions:

Inheritance: The concept of creating a class by including another as part of it.

Parent class: A class that is being inherited by another.

Child class: A class that inherits another.

name: Advance 3 : Class Polymorphism
description:
In this unit, you will learn about class polymorphism. It is the concept of how a class can inherit another and redefine its existing methods with its own implementations. The purpose is to make use of most of the existing attributes while customising some of them due to different requirements.

Programming definitions:

Polymorphism: The concept of redefining the methods in a class in order to vary them for different requirements.

Override: To redefine a method.

name: Advance 3 : Project
description:
Congratulations! This is the last project to obtain your certification for the Advanced curriculum. Give your best shot!

This project is a test of what you have learnt so far and the instructor will not be debugging your codes. You will be graded based on how well your program works.

You'll be using a Raspberry-Pi robot for output. You can choose to use a physical robot or the virtual robot when testing your code.

You will learn the following:-

Modules

  • LCD
  • Buzzer
  • Buttons
  • Ultrasonic Sensor
  • Colour Sensor
  • Motor

Coding concepts

  • Sequencing
  • Loops
  • If control statements
  • And/Or operators

name: Trial Class
description:
In this trial lesson, you will be introduced to the Raspberry Pi and related electronic components such a Grove Hat, Buzzer and LCD. The instructor will give a brief introduction to the Blockly UI and some basic blocks for controlling the Rasberry Pi robot. Students will then be asked to perform some tasks.


Programming Definitions:

The Raspberry Pi is a tiny and affordable computer that you can use to learn programming through fun, practical projects. Because of its affordability and functionality, Raspberry Pi is commonly used in tertiary education.


Blockly is the software which uses visual-programming (drag and drop) to teach programming. Blockly is integrated into our student portal and students will be able to control robots through the portal interface.

name: Basic 1 : Blockly Games
description:
In this lesson, you are given up to 3 different blockly games to explore (Maze, Bird, Turtle). 

Blockly games is one of the platforms the allows you to check your current programming competency level. You will be exploring it without help from the instructors and it does not matter if you are not able to solve the challenges.

name: Basic 1 : Sequence & Buzzer
description:
Programming Concept - Sequencing:

When solving problems and writing code, programmers begin by understanding the order in which actions occur. This is called sequencing. In this unit, we will practice sequencing in Google Blockly using the Buzzer module of your robot.

In Blockly, the blocks run from top to bottom. You must form your blocks in the right sequence to get the desired results.


Blocks:

Your robot is a Raspberry-Pi connected to different sensors via Groove-Hat.

      

In this unit, you will learn about the Buzzer. A buzzer is used for making sound

      

You can control the buzzer to make different sounds using a Note block or Tone block.

name: Intermediate 2 : List Basics
description:
Programming Concept - List:

A List is used to store a group of values, each identified with a running index starting from 1. Think of it as a building (list) where each level (index) has a room that houses someone (value).

      

Its flexibility makes it a powerful tool for handling and organizing data in code. In this unit, you'll learn how to create a list and read its contents.


Blocks:

Create a list by first creating a variable, then set it to a list of values using Create-list-with block. Each value has an index (the position), in blockly, it starts from 1.

      


You can also set the variable as an empty list first using Empty block and add values to it later.

      


Use the List-Get block to read an item from a list (it does not remove it from the list).

name: Advance 1 : Variable and Operations
description:

Programming definitions:

Variable: A variable is used to store a value that can be changed while the program runs. It can be given a customised name for easy referencing.

Data Type: The classification of a value such as string, integer, float, etc. Certain operators can only work on the certain data types. For example, an integer or float (number) can be divided but a string (text) can't.

Operator: Arithmetic and String Operators are used to compute results with variables or values, such as add, minus, etc. Python has specific symbols for various operators. Certain operators can only be used for a certain types of data.

description:

Programming definitions:

List: A data structure that stores values in a sequence.

Index: The position of each item in a list. It begins with 0 to an extremely large number (limited only by the computer hardware).

Length: The length of a list refers to the number of items in the list.

Append: To add an item to the end of a list.

Insert: To insert an item at any position of a list.

Pop: To remove an item from a list.

name: Advance 1 : String Manipulation
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to manipulate strings such as amending or extracting part of a string. Efficient string manipulation techniques are important parts of many algorithms.

Programming definitions:

Substring: Part of a string.

In Operator: Operator to check the existence of a substring in a string.

Length: Number of characters in a string. It includes invisible characters such as space, return key, etc.

Index: The position of a character in a string. It starts from 0 to length-1.

name: Advance 2 : Function
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to develop their program in modules call functions. Functions are useful in solution design as they break down the program into tasks. They can also be executed multiple times, thus, reducing the codes.

Programming definitions:

Function: A Python construct that groups a set of codes to accomplish specific tasks.

Parameter: Also known as an argument, an input parameter to a function is a value to be passed to it for processing.

Return: Results that are processed by a function are being passed back via a return statement.

Global Variable: A variable that is outside a function (in the main body of a program) but accessible by it.

Local Variable: A variable within a function is its local variable. A local variable is not accessible by other functions or in the main body.

name: Advance 2 : 2D List
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to create and manipulate a 2D list. 2D lists are useful for handling tabulated data or data that are represented on a 2D space.

Programming definitions:

Row and column: A 2D list can be viewed as a table with rows (horizontal streams of data) and columns (vertical streams of data).

Index: The position of each item in a list. A item in a 2D list will have a row index and column index, both of which begins at 0.

Length: A 2D list is implemented as a row of lists, each list has a column of items. The length of 2D list is, thus, the number of lists it contains (rows) and the length of each list is the number of items in it (columns). Note that it is possible for each row to have a list of different lengths.

name: Advance 2 : Dictionary
description:
In this unit, students will learn how to use dictionary. A dictionary is a storage type that allows the program to quickly access a value based on a unique key.

Programming definitions:

Key-value: A key is a unique identifier. It can be any single value (e.g. string, integer, float, etc) and is used to point to a value. A value in a dictionary can be more than a single value (e.g. a list, 2D list, etc)

Update: To add an item to a dictionary.

Pop: To remove an item from a dictionary.

Open: A file can be opened in different modes (e.g. for reading, writing, etc).

Close: After opening, a file has to be closed to ensure all data are properly saved. Python performs file closing automatically in certain file I/O construct.

Read: To read data from a file.

Write: To save data to a file.

name: Advance 2 : File Pointer

File pointer: A locator that exists when a file is opened. It remembers the last position where data has been read or written.

Tell: To extract the position of a file pointer.

Seek: To shift the file pointer to a location.

name: Advance 3 : Class
description:
In this unit, you will learn about OOP concept using classes in Python.

Programming definitions:

OOP: Object-Oriented Programming is a programming paradigm based on the concepts of "objects".

Class: A template codes consisting of variables and methods (functions). In order to execute the codes in a class, an object has to be created from it.

Object: An instance of a class. Each object has its own set of variables and methods. Its methods can manipulate its own variables without elaborate passing of parameters.

Method: Another name for function.

name: Advance 3 : Class Variable
description:
In this unit, you will learn how to create and use class variables. Different from object variables, class variables will not be duplicated by each object and are accessible by all.

Programming definitions:

Class Variable: A variable that belongs to a class. There is only one copy of the variable and it is not duplicated when an object is instanced. Hence, it acts like a global variable to the objects.

name: Advance 3 : Static Method
description:
In this unit, you will learn how to create and use static method. A static method is often designed as a method that does not need to process the object variables and hence, the object variables are not passed to it by the default manner.

Programming definitions:

Static method: A function belonging to a class (instead of an object). There is only one reference to the method and no multiples are created when an object is instanced. Object variables are thus, not passed to it by default.

Inheritance: The concept of creating a class by including another as part of it.

Parent class: A class that is being inherited by another.

Child class: A class that inherits another.

name: Advance 3 : Class Polymorphism
description:
In this unit, you will learn about class polymorphism. It is the concept of how a class can inherit another and redefine its existing methods with its own implementations. The purpose is to make use of most of the existing attributes while customising some of them due to different requirements.

Programming definitions:

Polymorphism: The concept of redefining the methods in a class in order to vary them for different requirements.

Override: To redefine a method.
